```go
package bookstore

import "sort"

// price is the cost of a single book in cents.
const price = 800

// groupPrice[k] is the cost in cents of a group of k distinct books,
// after the applicable discount.
var groupPrice = [6]int{
	0,
	800,
	1520,
	2160,
	2560,
	3000,
}

// Cost returns the total cost, in cents, of the given basket of books,
// after the largest possible discount.
// Books are identified by integers 1 through 5.
func Cost(books []int) int {
	counts := [5]int{}
	for _, book := range books {
		counts[book-1]++
	}
	return minCost(counts)
}

// minCost computes the cheapest way to partition the books identified by
// counts into groups of 1 to 5 distinct titles, using memoization.
func minCost(counts [5]int) int {
	sort.Slice(counts[:], func(i, j int) bool { return counts[i] > counts[j] })
	total := 0
	for _, c := range counts {
		total += c
	}
	if total == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if cached, ok := memo[counts]; ok {
		return cached
	}
	best := total * price // worst case: no discounts at all
	for mask := 1; mask < 1<<5; mask++ {
		size := bits.OnesCount8(uint8(mask))
		if size > 5 {
			continue
		}
		next := counts
		ok := true
		for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
			if mask&(1<<i) != 0 {
				if counts[i] == 0 {
					ok = false
					break
				}
				next[i]--
			}
		}
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if cost := groupPrice[size] + minCost(next); cost < best {
			best = cost
		}
	}
	memo[counts] = best
	return best
}
```

```go
package bookstore

import (
	"math/bits"
	"sort"
)

// price is the cost of a single book in cents.
const price = 800

// groupPrice[k] is the cost in cents of a group of k distinct books,
// after the discount for that group size.
var groupPrice = [6]int{
	0,
	800,  // 1 book: no discount
	1520, // 2 books: 5% off
	2160, // 3 books: 10% off
	2560, // 4 books: 20% off
	3000, // 5 books: 25% off
}

// memo caches minCost results keyed by the sorted per-title counts.
var memo = map[[5]int]int{}

// Cost returns the total cost, in cents, of the given basket of books,
// after the largest possible discount. Books 1 through 5 correspond to
// the five titles in the series.
func Cost(books []int) int {
	var counts [5]int
	for _, book := range books {
		counts[book-1]++
	}
	return minCost(counts)
}

// minCost returns the cheapest total cost of the books described by counts,
// where counts[i] is the number of copies of title i+1. It tries every
// possible first group (1 to 5 distinct titles) and memoizes on the
// canonical (sorted) remaining counts.
func minCost(counts [5]int) int {
	sort.Slice(counts[:], func(i, j int) bool { return counts[i] > counts[j] })

	total := 0
	for _, c := range counts {
		total += c
	}
	if total == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if cached, ok := memo[counts]; ok {
		return cached
	}

	best := total * price // upper bound: buy everything at full price
	for mask := 1; mask < 1<<5; mask++ {
		size := bits.OnesCount8(uint8(mask))
		next := counts
		possible := true
		for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
			if mask&(1<<i) != 0 {
				if counts[i] == 0 {
					possible = false
					break
				}
				next[i]--
			}
		}
		if possible && groupPrice[size]+minCost(next) < best {
			best = groupPrice[size] + minCost(next)
		}
	}

	memo[counts] = best
	return best
}
```

Why DP instead of the common greedy "maximize 5-groups" approach: the greedy fails on cases like `1,1,2,2,3,3,4,5`, where two 4-groups (5120) beat a 5+3 split (5560).
